readme:
# DeepMimic 四分量动作模仿奖励

## 1. 问题

DeepMimic 四分量动作模仿奖励：实现下列接口并通过数值、边界和实验检查。

实现姿态、角速度、末端与质心四项模仿奖励；姿态输入为预先计算的四元数测地角误差，不实现PPO、姿态解析或物理仿真。

## 2. 核心公式

$$
r^I=.65e^{-2\sum_j\theta_j^2}+.10e^{-.1\sum_j\|\Delta\dot q_j\|^2}+.15e^{-40\sum_e\|\Delta p_e\|^2}+.10e^{-10\|\Delta c\|^2}.
$$

## 3. 公式到代码

- `imitation_reward(pose_angles: Tensor, velocity_errors: Tensor, end_errors: Tensor, com_errors: Tensor) -> Tensor`

每个分量先对其所有关节/末端坐标平方求和，再应用论文特定指数系数。四项权重和为1，因此完美匹配奖励为1；相同末端偏差比角速度偏差受到更强惩罚。

## 4. 本题约定

pose_angles为(B,J)且在[0,pi]，velocity_errors为(B,J,3)，end_errors为(B,E,3)，com_errors为(B,3)，全部同dtype/device。返回(B,)奖励，不跨batch平均。所有误差保留梯度。

校验辅助函数已提供。浮点输入为有限 CPU float32/float64，不修改输入；非法形状、类型、范围或掩码必须抛出 `ValueError`。

## 5. 交互图与确定性实验

`experiment.py` 在固定输入上调用提交的全部接口，记录学习或采样曲线与末端指标。实验逻辑和阈值见 T3，输出同样用于可视化。

可视化由 `viz/gen.py` 生成；T3 将你的函数传入同一实验并记录真实指标。这是小规模确定性教学实验，不是机器人基准成绩。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 来源与延伸

- [DeepMimic: Example-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning of Physics-Based Character Skills](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02717) — Section 5.3 Reward Function: weighted pose, velocity, end-effector and center-of-mass imitation terms
- [Verified source](https://arxiv.org/html/1804.02717)

核验日期：2026-10-28。扩展到完整论文系统还需要本题范围中明确省略的模型、数据和环境。

# DeepMimic: 题解与易错点

每个分量先对其所有关节/末端坐标平方求和，再应用论文特定指数系数。四项权重和为1，因此完美匹配奖励为1；相同末端偏差比角速度偏差受到更强惩罚。

每个分量先对其所有关节/末端坐标平方求和，再应用论文特定指数系数。四项权重和为1，因此完美匹配奖励为1；相同末端偏差比角速度偏差受到更强惩罚。

先按公式确定归约轴、有效掩码和梯度路径，再将手算小例与实现逐项比较。测试中的独立预期值不调用参考答案。

## 测试捕获的错误

- End-effector position errors use the angular-velocity scale.
- Pose error averages joints instead of summing them.

## 实验范围

实现姿态、角速度、末端与质心四项模仿奖励；姿态输入为预先计算的四元数测地角误差，不实现PPO、姿态解析或物理仿真。

## 可重复实验记录

31个按误差比例1到0生成的动作候选；2关节、2末端，测量分项奖励，无训练器。要求完美匹配奖励1、初始<0.75、30次严格单调改善且全部在(0,1]。

判题固定seed=42。计算采用CPU float64、显式输入，涉及优化时使用普通梯度更新；不下载数据集或模型权重。原生PyTorch与真实Pyodide/NumPy-WASM执行同一套T0–T3测试。阈值针对本教学实验。

en.readme:
# DeepMimic Four-Component Motion Imitation Reward

## 1. Exercise goal

DeepMimic Four-Component Motion Imitation Reward: implement the interfaces below and verify numerical, boundary and experimental behavior.

Implement pose, angular-velocity, end-effector and center-of-mass imitation rewards. Pose inputs are precomputed quaternion geodesic angle errors; omit PPO, pose parsing and physical simulation.

## 2. Core equations

$$
r^I=.65e^{-2\sum_j\theta_j^2}+.10e^{-.1\sum_j\|\Delta\dot q_j\|^2}+.15e^{-40\sum_e\|\Delta p_e\|^2}+.10e^{-10\|\Delta c\|^2}.
$$

## 3. From equations to code

- `imitation_reward(pose_angles: Tensor, velocity_errors: Tensor, end_errors: Tensor, com_errors: Tensor) -> Tensor`

Within each component, sum squared joint/end-effector coordinates before applying its paper-specific exponential scale. The four weights sum to one, so perfect matching yields reward one. Equal end-effector errors are penalized more sharply than angular-velocity errors.

## 4. Contract and boundaries

Pose angles are (B,J) in [0,pi], velocity_errors (B,J,3), end_errors (B,E,3), com_errors (B,3), same dtype/device. Return (B,) rewards without batch averaging. Preserve error gradients.

Validation helpers are provided. All floating inputs are finite CPU float32/float64; do not mutate inputs. Invalid shape, dtype, range or mask arguments raise `ValueError`.

## 5. Deterministic experiment and visualization

`experiment.py` calls every submitted interface on fixed inputs and records a learning or sampling curve and terminal metrics. T3 states the behavioral thresholds; the visualization uses the same outputs.

The visualization is generated by `viz/gen.py`; T3 runs the same experiment with your functions and records its actual metrics. These are small deterministic teaching results, not a robot benchmark.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Sources and extensions

- [DeepMimic: Example-Guided Deep Reinforcement Learning of Physics-Based Character Skills](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02717) — Section 5.3 Reward Function: weighted pose, velocity, end-effector and center-of-mass imitation terms
- [Verified source](https://arxiv.org/html/1804.02717)

Verified 2026-10-28. Extending this operator to the full paper requires the omitted model, data and environment described in the scope above.
en.notes:
# DeepMimic: Solution notes

Identify reduction axes, validity masks and gradient paths from the equations before comparing a small hand calculation. Test oracles do not call the reference implementation.

## Mistakes caught by the tests

- End-effector position errors use the angular-velocity scale.
- Pose error averages joints instead of summing them.

## Experimental scope

Implement pose, angular-velocity, end-effector and center-of-mass imitation rewards. Pose inputs are precomputed quaternion geodesic angle errors; omit PPO, pose parsing and physical simulation.

## Reproducible protocol

31 motion candidates with error scale from one to zero, two joints and two end effectors; evaluate shaped rewards without training. Require perfect-match reward one, initial reward below .75, 30 strict improvements and all rewards in (0,1].

The judge fixes seed 42. All calculations use CPU float64, explicit inputs and plain gradient updates where applicable; no datasets or model weights are downloaded. Native PyTorch and actual Pyodide/NumPy-WASM run the same T0–T3 suite. Thresholds refer to this teaching adaptation.
